messages:
Anna K: quick heads-up — opened a tiny PR updating Dedicated provisioning doc to clarify fallback routing + SLA wording. Link: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1234 :paperclip:
Anna K: main ask: can folks scan the autoscale policy example under 'burst & cool-down' and the tenant isolation example? I added a YAML snippet for tenant labels, not 100% on the phrasing 'best-effort isolation'.
Mike R: looking now :eyes:
Tara L: re: 'best-effort isolation' — I'd avoid that phrasing in public docs. Maybe 'no guaranteed isolation' or 'soft isolation' is clearer and less SLA-y. also call out eviction/preemption windows briefly.
Sahil D: small nit — the runtime API uses `isolation`, while older SDKs still accept `isolation_level`. If we show a config snippet, include both keys and comment the difference.
Anna K: good catch, will add both with explanatory comment. updating now.
Anna K: ```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  cool_down_sec: 120
fallback:
  enabled: true
  priority: regional, capacity_tier
tenant_config:
  isolation: tenant  # runtime field
  isolation_level: tenant  # legacy SDK mapping
```
Jess P: small wording suggestion for the SLA blurb: don't use 'SLA-backed' unless it's a paid/reserved tier. maybe 'reserved tiers include SLA guarantees' or 'SLA available for reserved capacity' to avoid confusion.
Docs Bot: link-checker: found 1 broken link — /docs/preemption-handbook (404).
Anna K: thanks — fixed the link and pushed a tiny follow-up commit.
Mike R: LGTM :thumbsup:
Tara L: also added a short note about which metrics to monitor (tail latency and queue depth) — I'll follow up with an example snippet in another PR.
Anna K: perfect. planning to merge in ~10m unless anyone objects.
Anna K: (if you want to leave a short review comment instead of full review, lmk — trying to keep this fast)
